docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: rmfakecloud is a clone of the cloud sync the remarkable tablet is using, in case you want to sync/backup your files and have full control of the hosting/storage environment.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• File synchronization (compatible with revisions 1.0 and 1.5)
  • Integrations with external file sources: WebDAV, FTP, Dropbox, a local directory, ICS calendars and a messaging webhook
  • Send document by email
  • Handwriting recognition
  • Screen sharing
  • Passcode (PIN) reset approval (reMarkable 1 / reMarkable 2 only)
  • Read on reMarkable browser extension

It comes with a web interface that lets you:

  • Generate the one time code to connect a device
  • Browse, upload and delete documents, create folders
  • Download documents as PDF, including your annotations
  • Manage your integrations
  • Watch a screen share
  • Change your password and enable two-factor login
  • Manage users (admins)

docs.title: Browser Extension Support
docs.text:
As of commit a62153e, the Read on reMarkable Chrome extension is supported by rmfakecloud. Of course, the extension needs to be modified to connect to your cloud.

  1. Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store.

  2. Find the extension directory:

  3. Go to chrome://extensions in your browser, find "Read on reMarkable" in the list, and take note of the ID.
    • Mine is bfhkfdnddlhfippjbflipboognpdpoeh.
  4. Go to chrome://version in your browser, and take note of the "Profile Path".
    • Mine is /home/murchu27/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Default (Linux).

  5. Your extension directory will be {Profile Path}/Extensions/{ID}/{some version number}.

    • Mine is /home/murchu27/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Default/Extensions/bfhkfdnddlhfippjbflipboognpdpoeh/1.2.0_0.

  6. Within the extension directory, replace any instances of https://internal.cloud.remarkable.com and https://webapp-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com/ with the URL of your cloud (same as the STORAGE_URL used by the tablet). You will need to do this in manifest.json, and any of the .js files.

  7. If you are using Linux, you can save the below script as, e.g., rmfakecloud-patch.sh. mycloud=$1 find ./ -type f -exec sed -i "s/https:\/\/internal.cloud.remarkable.com/$mycloud/g" {} \; find ./ -type f -exec sed -i "s/https:\/\/webapp-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com/$mycloud/g" {} \;

  8. Make this script executable with chmod +x rmfakecloud-patch.sh.

  9. Run the script, passing in the URL of your cloud, e.g., ./rmfakecloud-patch.sh http://mycloud.com.

  10. Reload the extension in your browser:

  11. Go to chrome://extensions in your browser. Enable "Developer mode" using the toggle at the top right.
  12. Click the newly appeared "Load unpacked" button, a dialogue box will open.

  13. Navigate to the extension directory (the same one as in the step above), and click "Open".

  14. Try using the extension. Webpages should be sent to your tablet!

See #67 for the original discussion of this feature.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The configuration is made through environment variables.

docs.title: General configuration
docs.text: Variable name Description JWT_SECRET_KEY The secret key used to sign the authentication token.If you don't provide it, a random secret is generated, invalidating all connections established previously to be closed.A good secret is for example: openssl rand -base64 48 STORAGE_URL It controls whether file upload/download goes through the local proxy or to an external server. It's the full address (protocol, host, port, path) of rmfakecloud as visible from the tablet, especially if the host is behind a reverse proxy or in a container. Example: http://192.168.2.3:3000 (default: https://local.appspot.com), on SW 3.15 only https without port will work PORT listening port number (default: 3000) DATADIR Set data/files directory (default: data/ in current dir) TLS_CERT Path to a certificate, together with TLS_KEY rmfakecloud serves HTTPS itself TLS_KEY Path to the certificate's private key LOGLEVEL Set the log verbosity. Default is info, set to debug for more logging or warn, error for less LOGFORMAT json for JSON logs, default is text RM_LOGFILE Additionally write the log to this file OPEN_REGISTRATION Allow creating users via POST /ui/api/register, only from localhost (default: false) RM_HTTPS_COOKIE For the UI, force cookies to be available only via https RM_SESSION_TTL How long a login to the web UI lasts, e.g. 720h for 30 days when it's installed as an app (default: 24h). Changing the password ends all logins RM_TRUST_PROXY Take the client ip address from X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP set by a reverse proxy. 1 trusts proxies on loopback and private networks, or set a comma separated list of proxy IPs/CIDRs, e.g. 203.0.113.10,2001:db8::/64 (default: off) HASH_SCHEMA_VERSION Hash tree schema version: "3" or "4" (default: 3)

docs.title: Handwriting recognition
docs.text:
To use the handwriting recognition feature, you need first to create a free account on https://developer.myscript.com/ (up to 2000 free recognitions per month).

Then you'll obtains an application key and its corresponding HMAC to give to rmfakecloud:

Variable name Description RMAPI_HWR_APPLICATIONKEY Application key obtained from myscript RMAPI_HWR_HMAC HMAC obtained from myscript RMAPI_HWR_LANG_OVERRIDE Optional: Use this if you want your handwriting to be recognized as a different language. This variable accepts a locale code (e.g., zh_CN). Refer to this page for supported languages. RMAPI_HWR_HOST Optional: Custom myScript host URL (default: https://cloud.myscript.com). Supports http/https and custom ports.

docs.title: OCR for scanned PDFs
docs.text:
PDFs uploaded through the web UI or the upload API get a searchable text layer when an OCR service is configured. The OCR runs in the background, the document is replaced once it is done and the tablet syncs it again. PDFs that already contain text stay as they are. See Docker for the service.

Variable name Description RM_OCR_URL URL of the OCR service, e.g. http://ocr:8080. Empty: no OCR

docs.title: Email settings
docs.text:
To be able to send email from your reMarkable, fill the following variables:

Variable name Description RM_SMTP_SERVER The SMTP server address in host:port format RM_SMTP_USERNAME The username/email for login RM_SMTP_PASSWORD Plaintext password (application password should work) RM_SMTP_FROM Custom From: header for the mails (eg. ReMarkable self-hosted <remarkable@my.example.net>). If this override is set, the user's email address is instead put as Reply-To RM_SMTP_HELO Custom HELO, if your email provider needs it RM_SMTP_NOTLS don't use tls RM_SMTP_STARTTLS use starttls command, should be combined with NOTLS. in most cases port 587 should be used RM_SMTP_INSECURE_TLS If set, don't check the server certificate (not recommended)

docs.title: Screen sharing
docs.text: Screen sharing streams your tablet display to a browser via WebRTC. There are two signaling modes depending on your tablet's software version.

docs.title: REST-based (reMarkable OS 3.27+)
docs.text:
Starting with OS 3.27, the tablet can use REST-based signaling instead of MQTT. No additional setup is required, screen sharing works out of the box.

Start a screen share session from the sharing menu on your tablet, then open the Screen Share page in the rmfakecloud web UI. The page automatically finds the active session and connects.

Variable name Description ICE_SERVERS JSON array of WebRTC ICE servers. Default: Google STUN server. Format: [{"urls":["stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"]}] or with TURN: [{"urls":["turn:turn.example.com:3478"],"username":"user","credential":"pass"}]

Without ICE_SERVERS set, a public Google STUN server is used, which works when the tablet and browser / app are on the same network. If you want to screenshare across the internet, you may need a TURN server.

docs.title: MQTT-based (reMarkable OS < 3.27)
docs.text:
Older tablet software uses MQTT for screen share signaling. This requires additional configuration:

Variable name Description MQTT_PORT Port for MQTT broker (default: 8883) ICE_SERVERS JSON array of WebRTC ICE servers. Default: none. Format: [{"urls":["stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"]}] or with TURN: [{"urls":["turn:turn.example.com:3478"],"username":"user","credential":"pass"}] TLS_CERT path/to/cert, MQTT with TLS, unless the reverse proxy terminates TLS TLS_KEY /path/to/key, MQTT with TLS, unless the reverse proxy terminates TLS

The tablet connects to vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering:443 with TLS, see device setup for the hosts entry and the certificate. Either the reverse proxy terminates TLS (below), or rmfakecloud does with TLS_CERT/TLS_KEY, then the web UI and API are served over HTTPS as well. Desktop apps may not use the system certificate store for MQTT. Without ICE_SERVERS set, screen sharing will work over USB and if the tablet and desktop app are on the same network.

docs.title: Reverse proxy for MQTT (Screen sharing)
docs.text: MQTT uses TCP with TLS. Typical reverse proxies require TCP stream forwarding rather than HTTP proxying.

docs.title: nginx (stream module)
docs.text:
stream {
    upstream mqtt {
        server rmfakecloud:8883;
    }

    server {
        listen 443;
        proxy_pass mqtt;
        proxy_connect_timeout 5s;
    }
}

docs.title: Traefik (TCP router)
docs.text:
tcp:
  routers:
    mqtt:
      rule: "HostSNI(`*`)"
      service: mqtt
      entryPoints:
        - mqtt
  services:
    mqtt:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - address: "rmfakecloud:8883"

entryPoints:
  mqtt:
    address: ":443"

docs.title: Traefik on Kubernetes, next to the web UI
docs.text:
To share port 443 with the web UI, route by SNI on the existing websecure entry point. Traefik terminates TLS with the tablet's proxy.crt/proxy.key (as a TLS secret) and passes plain MQTT on. Not tested end to end yet:

apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: IngressRouteTCP
metadata:
  name: rmfakecloud-mqtt
spec:
  entryPoints: [websecure]
  routes:
    - match: HostSNI(`vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering`)
      services:
        - name: rmfakecloud
          port: 8883
  tls:
    secretName: rmfakecloud-mqtt-tls

docs.title: With Docker
docs.text:
You can evaluate the program with:

docker run -it --rm -p 3000:3000 ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud

For normal usage, you need a volume to store user configuration and documents:

docker run -it --rm -p 3000:3000 -p 8883:8883 -v ./data:/data -e JWT_SECRET_KEY='something' ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud

Explore others configuration variables on the dedicated page.

docs.title: docker-compose file
docs.text:
services:
  rmfakecloud:
    image: ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud
    container_name: rmfakecloud
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
      - "8883:8883"
    env_file:
      - env
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

In this example, an external file named env is provided that contains the environment variables. Any of the ways to set environment variables for docker compose will work.

For the possible environment variables, please have a look in the configuration section.

docs.title: OCR for scanned PDFs
docs.text:
The image ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud-ocr runs OCRmyPDF and adds a text layer to uploaded scans, so they can be searched on the tablet and in the web UI. Add it next to rmfakecloud and point RM_OCR_URL to it:

services:
  rmfakecloud:
    # ...
    environment:
      RM_OCR_URL: http://ocr:8080

  ocr:
    image: ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud-ocr
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      OCR_LANGUAGES: deu+eng

The service has no authentication, don't publish its port.

OCR_LANGUAGES takes the Tesseract languages joined with +, the image contains deu and eng. For other languages, build your own image on top of it:

FROM ghcr.io/hb9hil/rmfakecloud-ocr
USER root
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tesseract-ocr-fra && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
USER nobody

docs.title: Rebuild the image
docs.text: make image

docs.title: Access rmfakecloud from outside your local network safely
docs.text:
This guide explains how to get your reMarkable to access rmfakecloud from outside your local network, without exposing rmfakecloud directly to the internet or using VPNs, with a Cloudflare Tunnel and client authentication.

A domain name is needed for this setup, otherwise it's free. It will probably ask for a payment method to be added, but no charges will be made. The domain's nameservers also will need to point to Cloudflare.

Note

Data is encrypted between the reMarkable tablet and Cloudflare and between Cloudflare and your local network, but not on Cloudflare.

docs.title: 1. Create a Cloudflare account and add a payment method
docs.text: Create a Cloudflare account and add a payment method. No charges will be made as everything is done within the free plan.

docs.title: 2. Add your domain to Cloudflare
docs.text:
In your account home, click "Onboard a domain" and enter your domain name. With "Quick scan for DNS records" enabled, Cloudflare will import your existing DNS records. Click "Continue" and select the free plan.

If you have an email set up with this domain or don't want other services to be proxied, set the corresponding records to "DNS only".

docs.title: 3. Change your domain nameservers
docs.text: Follow the instructions you see on screen to change your domain's nameservers to the ones provided by Cloudflare. This is done on your domain registrar's website.

docs.title: 4. Set up a tunnel
docs.text:
In the Zero Trust dashboard (Cloudflare One), go to Networks > Connectors and click "Create a tunnel".

Select "Cloudflared" tunnel type and follow the instructions to install a connector in your preferred environment. When you see an entry in the connectors list with status "Connected", that means the connector is running and ready.

In the "Route tunnel" step, set the subdomain you want to use to access rmfakecloud and your domain (for example, rmfakecloud and example.com to access the instance in rmfakecloud.example.com). For the rest of the guide, replace rmfakecloud.example.com with your chosen subdomain and domain.

In Service, set type to HTTPS and URL to a placeholder like placeholder (because we haven't set up authentication yet), then click "Save".

docs.title: 5. Generate a client certificate
docs.text:
In the domain dashboard, go to SSL/TLS > Client Certificates and click "Create Certificate".

The default options are fine, so click "Create" (although 10 years validity is a lot, may be a good idea to set it to a shorter period).

Copy the text under "Certificate" and save it to a file client.crt, then copy the text under "Private Key" and save it to a file client.key. You can use whatever names you want for these files, just remember to use the names you choose instead of client.crt and client.key.

docs.title: 6. Get the certificate serial number
docs.text:
If you're on Linux or macOS (or if you have OpenSSL installed in Windows), you can run this command to get the get the serial number of the certificate:

openssl x509 -in client.crt -noout -serial | cut -d "=" -f2

On Windows, open properties of file client.crt, go to the "Details" tab, look for the "Serial number" field and copy its value.

The serial number has to be in uppercase hexadecimal format without spaces or colons, e.g. 123456789ABCDEF123456789ABCDEF123456789A. If it's not, convert it before using it in the next step.

docs.title: 7. Set up a rule to block everything except requests with the client certificate
docs.text:
Note

Cloudflare Zero Trust supports mTLS, but it's an enterprise only feature. We can set a security rule to achieve the same effect.

Go to Security > Security rules, click "Create rule" and "Custom rules".

Set whatever name you want for the rule, e.g. "Require my rM client certificate".

Click "Edit expression" and enter the following expression, replacing SERIAL_NUMBER with the serial number obtained in the previous step and rmfakecloud.example.com with your chosen subdomain and domain:

(
    cf.tls_client_auth.cert_serial ne "SERIAL_NUMBER"
    or not cf.tls_client_auth.cert_verified
    or not cf.tls_client_auth.cert_presented
    or cf.tls_client_auth.cert_revoked
)
and http.host contains "rmfakecloud.example.com"

Info on these fields can be found here.

Set the action to "Block" and click "Deploy".

docs.title: 8. Point the application route to your rmfakecloud instance
docs.text:
Back to the Zero Trust dashboard, go to Networks > Connectors, click on your tunnel and the "Edit" button.

Go to the "Published application routes" tab, click on the route you created earlier and edit it.

In the URL field, remove the placeholder set earlier (placeholder) and enter the local address of your rmfakecloud instance, e.g. http://192.168.1.100:3000. This will vary depending on your setup.

docs.title: 9. Check if it's working as expected
docs.text:
You can check if everything is working as expected running these commands in the directory where you saved the certificate and key files.

This command should return the normal rmfakecloud HTML response (won't work on Windows):

curl --cert client.crt --key client.key https://rmfakecloud.example.com

This command should return the HTML of a Cloudflare block page:

curl https://rmfakecloud.example.com

In Windows, if you have OpenSSL installed, you can to combine the certificate and key into a single .pfx file and then make the request with it. This should return the normal rmfakecloud HTML response:

openssl pkcs12 -export -out client.pfx -inkey client.key -in client.crt
curl --cert client.pfx https://rmfakecloud.example.com

docs.title: 10. Configure your reMarkable to use the new address and certificate
docs.text:
Copy the client.crt and client.key files to /home/root/rmfakecloud with your preferred method (scp, WinSCP, etc.).

Install rmfakecloud-proxy as the installation instructions explain.

When asked for the cloud url, enter your public address. In this case, https://rmfakecloud.example.com.

In path to client certificate file, enter client.crt. Do not enter as a path, only use the name of the file you have placed in the /home/root/rmfakecloud folder.

In path to client key file, enter client.key. Again, only enter as a filename, not the path.

You should now be able to sync your reMarkable from outside your local network. Pairing does not work using mTLS authentication, and you will run into a cloudflare block screen. Make sure to pair beforehand, or disable the security rule temporarily for pairing.

docs.title: Fail2ban
docs.text:
rmfakecloud itself blocks an IP address for 15 minutes after 5 failed web UI logins. Behind a reverse proxy this needs RM_TRUST_PROXY=1, otherwise all clients share the proxy's address.

For a public server fail2ban adds some security by banning ip's after few (configurable) failed login attempts. Assuming rmfakecloud is running in docker via systemd and logs to the syslog (journalctl) and fail2ban is already installed and setup. Instructions install and setup fail2ban in the documentation of the used operating system or at https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban#installation . rmfakecloud needs to trust the reverse proxy in use, i.e. add RM_TRUST_PROXY=1 (proxy on loopback or a private network) or the proxy's IP to the docker environment, see configuration.

docs.title: Jail
docs.text:
First it is necessary to define a jail, e.g. in /etc/fail2ban/jail.local:

[rmfakecloud]
enabled   = true
filter   = rmfakecloud
action   = iptables-multiport[name=HTTP, port="http,https"]
journalmatch = _SYSTEMD_UNIT=docker-rmfakecloud.service

where it is necessary to change "docker-rmfakecloud.service" to the name of the systemd service used to run the server and the ban action appropriate to the setup of the host.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Additionally the filter

[Definition]
failregex = ^.*, login failed ip:\s+<ADDR>.*$

in /etc/fail2ban/filter.d/rmfakecloud.conf tells fail2ban which lines are relevant. Wrong passwords and wrong two-factor codes both match it.

After creating the necessary configuration, restarting fail2ban loads the changes.

docs.title: Kubernetes with Helm
docs.text:
The chart is published with every release:

helm install rmfakecloud oci://ghcr.io/hb9hil/charts/rmfakecloud --version X.Y.Z -f values.yaml

It runs one replica: notifications to the tablets, pairing codes and screen sharing live in the memory of the process, a second pod would not see them.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
All options with comments are in helm/values.yaml. A typical setup behind an ingress with cert-manager:

env:
  STORAGE_URL: https://rm.example.com
  RM_SMTP_SERVER: smtp.example.com:587
  RM_SMTP_USERNAME: rmfakecloud@example.com

existingSecret: rmfakecloud

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: traefik
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt
  host: rm.example.com
  tlsSecretName: rm-example-com-tls

ocr:
  enabled: true
  • env takes any setting from the configuration as environment variable. STORAGE_URL must be the public https URL without port.
  • existingSecret holds the sensitive settings: JWT_SECRET_KEY, RM_SMTP_PASSWORD, RMAPI_HWR_APPLICATIONKEY, RMAPI_HWR_HMAC, ICE_SERVERS. Without it, the chart creates a secret with a random JWT_SECRET_KEY and keeps it on upgrades. This uses lookup, which works with helm and Flux but not with Argo CD; set existingSecret there.
  • ocr.enabled adds the OCR service as a second container in the pod, rmfakecloud reaches it on localhost.

docs.title: Updates without downtime
docs.text:
The default strategy Recreate fits a ReadWriteOnce volume. On a ReadWriteMany volume (e.g. CephFS, NFS) the new pod can start before the old one stops, rmfakecloud locks the sync root with flock across pods:

strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
persistence:
  storageClass: ceph-fs
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]

docs.title: Screen sharing
docs.text: The chart only serves HTTP. Screen sharing up to tablet software 3.26 needs MQTT on port 8883, see Traefik on Kubernetes.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
To be able to compile from source, you'll need the following dependencies:

  • nodejs version 26 or newer
  • go version 1.26 or newer
  • make

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hb9hil/rmfakecloud
cd rmfakecloud
make all

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
1. Download the binary for your system from the releases (or take the one you built from the dist folder), copy it to /usr/local/bin and rename it to rmfakecloud e.g. cp rmfakecloud-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/rmfakecloud or scp rmfakecloud-linux-armv7 raspberry:/usr/local/bin/rmfakecloud
  2. Setup the service to run with your init system. See below for examples
  3. Create and modify the configuration file. See below for examples
  4. Create the library folder you specified in your configuration file. e.g. mkdir /usr/local/lib/rmfakecloud
  5. Enable and start the service with your init system. e.g. rc-update add rmfakecloud && service start rmfakecloud or systemctl enable --now rmfakecloud

docs.title: OpenRC
docs.text:
/etc/init.d/rmfakecloud

#!/sbin/openrc-run

name="rmfakecloud"
command="/usr/local/bin/rmfakecloud"
command_args=""
pidfile="/var/run/rmfakecloud.pid"
command_background="yes"
output_log="/var/log/messages"
error_log="/var/log/messages"
depend() {
    need net localmount
}

/etc/conf.d/rmfakecloud

# Basic settings
export JWT_SECRET_KEY=SOME_KEY
export STORAGE_URL=http(s)://host.where.rmfakecloud.is.running
export PORT=80
export DATADIR=/usr/local/lib/rmfakecloud
export LOGLEVEL=info
# uncomment if using TLS
#export PORT=443
#export TLS_KEY=/path/to/somekey
#export TLS_CERT=/path/to/somecert
#export RM_HTTPS_COOKIE=1

# Email
export RM_SMTP_SERVER=smtp.gmail.com:465
export RM_SMTP_USERNAME=MY_EMAIL_ADDRESS
export RM_SMTP_PASSWORD=MY_SMTP_OR_APP_PASSWORD
# Handwriting recognition
export RMAPI_HWR_APPLICATIONKEY=SOME_KEY
export RMAPI_HWR_HMAC=SOME_KEY

Make sure to replace SOME_KEY by the return of openssl rand -base64 48, see configuration.

If using GMail, ensure you enable 2FA on that Google account, generate a GMail app password (https://myaccount.google.com/u/0/apppasswords), and provide the app password instead of the account password above.

docs.title: systemd
docs.text:
rmfakecloud.service

[Unit]
Description=rmfakecloud
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rmfakecloud
EnvironmentFile=/etc/rmfakecloud.conf

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

rmfakecloud.conf

JWT_SECRET_KEY=SOME_KEY
STORAGE_URL=http(s)://host.where.rmfakecloud.is.running
PORT=80
DATADIR=/usr/local/lib/rmfakecloud
LOGLEVEL=info
# uncomment if using TLS
#PORT=443
#TLS_KEY=/path/to/somekey
#TLS_CERT=/path/to/somecert
#RM_HTTPS_COOKIE=1

# Email
RM_SMTP_SERVER=smtp.gmail.com:465
RM_SMTP_USERNAME=MY_EMAIL_ADDRESS
RM_SMTP_PASSWORD=MY_SMTP_OR_APP_PASSWORD
# Handwriting recognition
RMAPI_HWR_APPLICATIONKEY=SOME_KEY
RMAPI_HWR_HMAC=SOME_KEY

Make sure to replace SOME_KEY with the output of openssl rand -base64 48, see configuration.

If using GMail, ensure you enable 2FA on that Google account, generate a GMail app password (https://myaccount.google.com/u/0/apppasswords), and provide the app password instead of the account password above.

docs.title: Apache
docs.text:
rmfakecloud listens on plain HTTP (localhost:3000 in this example), Apache terminates HTTPS in front of it. It needs the modules proxy, proxy_http, proxy_wstunnel, rewrite, headers and ssl.

<VirtualHost *:443>
  ServerName rmfakecloud.example.com

  SSLEngine on
  SSLCertificateFile    /etc/letsencrypt/live/rmfakecloud.example.com/fullchain.pem
  SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/letsencrypt/live/rmfakecloud.example.com/privkey.pem

  ProxyRequests Off
  ProxyPreserveHost On
  RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https"

  # the tablet's sync notifications use a websocket
  RewriteEngine on
  RewriteCond %{HTTP:Upgrade} websocket [NC]
  RewriteCond %{HTTP:Connection} upgrade [NC]
  RewriteRule ^/?(.*) "ws://localhost:3000/$1" [P,L]

  ProxyPass        / http://localhost:3000/
  ProxyPassReverse / http://localhost:3000/
</VirtualHost>

apachectl configtest checks the config, apachectl graceful loads it.

rmfakecloud configuration:

STORAGE_URL=https://rmfakecloud.example.com
RM_TRUST_PROXY=1     # client ip from X-Forwarded-For, for the login limiter and fail2ban
RM_HTTPS_COOKIE=1    # the web UI cookie only over https

Don't expose port 3000 directly once HTTPS works.

On the tablet, use https://rmfakecloud.example.com as the cloud url when installing rmfakecloud-proxy.

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
rmfakecloud listens on plain HTTP (localhost:3000 in this example), nginx terminates HTTPS in front of it.

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name rmfakecloud.example.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/rmfakecloud.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/rmfakecloud.example.com/privkey.pem;

    # large PDFs and notebooks
    client_max_body_size 200M;
    proxy_buffering off;
    proxy_request_buffering off;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:3000/;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_redirect http:// https://;

        # the tablet's sync notifications use a websocket
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
    }
}

rmfakecloud configuration:

STORAGE_URL=https://rmfakecloud.example.com
RM_TRUST_PROXY=1     # client ip from X-Forwarded-For, for the login limiter and fail2ban
RM_HTTPS_COOKIE=1    # the web UI cookie only over https

Don't expose port 3000 directly once HTTPS works.

On the tablet, use https://rmfakecloud.example.com as the cloud url when installing rmfakecloud-proxy.

Screen sharing over MQTT (tablet software < 3.27) needs a TCP stream proxy, see configuration.

docs.title: Desktop Client
docs.text:
This page covers using the official reMarkable desktop apps with a self-hosted rmfakecloud.

There are two approaches:

  1. Manual setup (edit the hosts file).
  2. Patch the desktop app (RMHook or RMHook-Win).

docs.title: Manual Setup (Hosts File)
docs.text: This method keeps the official desktop app but redirects traffic by editing the hosts file. It is useful if you do not want to patch the app.

docs.title: macOS /etc/hosts
docs.text:
1. Open /etc/hosts as root.
  2. Point the reMarkable cloud domains to your rmfakecloud IP.

Example (replace 203.0.113.5 with your rmfakecloud public IP):

203.0.113.5 hwr-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com
203.0.113.5 service-manager-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com
203.0.113.5 local.appspot.com
203.0.113.5 my.remarkable.com
203.0.113.5 ping.remarkable.com
203.0.113.5 internal.cloud.remarkable.com
203.0.113.5 webapp-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering
203.0.113.5 eu.tectonic.remarkable.com
203.0.113.5 backtrace-proxy.cloud.remarkable.engineering

This list follows the guidance in the "Getting Traffic To The Server" section from: https://blog.scottlabs.io/2025/10/selfhosting-a-remarkable-cloud/#getting-traffic-to-the-server

docs.title: Windows hosts file
docs.text:
1. Open C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts in an elevated editor (Run as Administrator).
  2. Add the same domain entries as above, pointing to your rmfakecloud IP.

docs.title: Linux /etc/hosts
docs.text:
1. Open /etc/hosts as root.
  2. Add the same domain entries as above, pointing to your rmfakecloud IP.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: • Add the CA certificate to macOS Keychain and server.crt / server.key installed on rmfakecloud.

docs.title: macOS Desktop via RMHook
docs.text:
If you only need to point the official macOS desktop app at your self-hosted instance, you can patch it with RMHook. The tool injects a custom dylib into the reMarkable Desktop bundle so all cloud traffic is redirected to your rmfakecloud host without editing /etc/hosts and adding CA certificates.

There is an auto script provided on the repo as well as a manual setup.

docs.title: Auto Installation
docs.text:
Run in a terminal:

bash <(curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NohamR/RMHook/refs/heads/main/scripts/auto-install.sh)

docs.title: Windows / Linux via RMHook-Win
docs.text:
RMHook-Win is a Windows port of RMHook for the reMarkable Desktop application. It builds a proxy DLL that hooks Qt network APIs and redirects reMarkable cloud traffic to a self-hosted rmfakecloud server.

RMHook-Win intercepts the reMarkable Desktop app's Qt networking layer and patches outgoing requests to the configured host and port. It is designed for the Windows reMarkable Desktop client and uses a DLL proxy for paho-mqtt3as.dll.

docs.title: Auto Installation
docs.text:
Run in a PowerShell terminal with administrator privileges:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NohamR/RMHook-Win/refs/heads/main/scripts/download-and-install.ps1 | iex

docs.title: Device Setup
docs.text:
There are several ways to make it work, choose whatever works for you

Important

Whenever the tablet receives a system update, the cloud connection will break, and will have to be reenabled.

docs.title: toltec
docs.text:
Install using toltec.

opkg install rmfakecloud-proxy
rmfakecloudctl set-upstream <URL>
rmfakecloudctl enable

The <URL> above has to be the same as in the STORAGE_URL server configuration.

docs.title: rmfakecloud-proxy script
docs.text:
Get the installer from: rmfakecloud-proxy scp to the device and run it

reMarkable 1 & reMarkable 2

scp installer-rm12.sh root@10.11.99.1:
ssh root@10.11.99.1
chmod +x ./installer-rm12.sh
./installer-rm12.sh install

reMarkable Paper Pro & Paper Pro Move

scp installer-rmpro.sh root@10.11.99.1:
ssh root@10.11.99.1
chmod +x ./installer-rmpro.sh
./installer-rmpro.sh install

docs.title: Installing a proxy on devices
docs.text:
A reverse proxy rmfakecloud-proxy has to be installed run rmfakecloud on whichever port you want, you can use either HTTP (not recommended) or HTTPS, generate a new cert for the url you chose e.g with Let's Encrypt

Steps (done by the automagic scripts):

  • generate a CA and host certificate for *.appspot.com
  • create the CA folder: mkdir -p /usr/local/share/ca-certificates
  • copy the CA.crt file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and run update-ca-certificates
  • modify the hosts file /etc/hosts
  • Run a reverse https proxy on the rm tablet as a service, e.g. secure,
  • stop xochitl systemctl stop xochitl
  • add the following entries to /etc/hosts
127.0.0.1 hwr-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com
127.0.0.1 service-manager-production-dot-remarkable-production.appspot.com
127.0.0.1 local.appspot.com
127.0.0.1 my.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 ping.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 internal.cloud.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 eu.tectonic.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 backtrace-proxy.cloud.remarkable.engineering
127.0.0.1 dev.ping.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 dev.tectonic.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 dev.internal.cloud.remarkable.com
127.0.0.1 eu.internal.tctn.cloud.remarkable.com
  • set the address of your api host:port in the reverse proxy secure -cert proxy.crt -key proxy.key http(s)://host_where_the_api_is_running:someport or use the provided systemd unit file and put the config in proxycfg
  • set the STORAGE_URL to point to this address (this thing the device can resolve/see e.g the reverse proxy, public dns etc)
  • run the host
  • run fixsync.sh on the device to mark all files as new (not to be deleted from the device)
  • start xochitl systemctl start xochitl

Windows/Mac Desktop Client:

  • modify the hosts file (\system32\drivers\etc\hosts) add the same entries as on the tablet
  • run a reverse proxy on the host or somewhere else pointing it to rmfakecloud with the same certs
  • profit

PROS: easy setup, you can use whichever port you want, you can get a real trusted ca cert from let's encrypt, if running in a trusted network you may chose to use HTTP CONS: you have to configure HTTPS on the host yourself, additional Desktop config

docs.title: Modify device /etc/hosts
docs.text:
Connect to the host directly, without a reverse proxy, with HTTPS on :443

Steps:

  • generate the certs from Variant 1, you get them (proxy.crt, proxy.key, ca.crt) and trust the ca.crt
  • run rmfakecloud with:
TLS_KEY=proxy.key
TLS_CERT=proxy.crt
STORAGE_URL=https://local.appspot.com
  • modify /etc/hosts but use the rmfakecloud's ip instead of 127.0.0.1

Windows/Mac Desktop Client:

  • trust the ca.crt (add it to Trusted Root CA, use cert.msc)
  • modify the hosts file (\system32\drivers\etc\hosts) add the same entries as on the tablet
  • profit

PROS: you can use the Windows/Mac clients, no need for a proxy on the device CONS: a bit harder to setup, each host has to trust the ca and modify the hosts file, you have to use port 443

docs.title: Edit router DNS entries
docs.text:
Same as the previous method, but instead of modifying any hosts file, make the changes on your DNS/router:

  • add the host entries directly on your router (Hosts in OpenWRT)
  • trust the ca.crt
  • profit

PROS: a bit easier, you can you even the mobile apps if you manage to install the root ca CONS: you can't use the official cloud anymore due to the mangled DNS

docs.title: Screen sharing (software up to 3.26)
docs.text:
Up to software 3.26 the tablet signals screen sharing over MQTT with TLS. It always connects to vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering on port 443. The hostname is built in: the tablet doesn't ask rmfakecloud for it, and rmfakecloud-proxy doesn't cover it. Without the steps below, screen sharing silently does nothing.

From software 3.27 on, screen sharing uses the normal API through rmfakecloud-proxy and needs none of this.

Note

These steps follow what the tablet does on 3.26, they are not yet tested end to end.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
1. Make port 443 of <your rmfakecloud ip> pass the MQTT connection on to rmfakecloud's MQTT port (MQTT_PORT, default 8883). If the web UI already uses port 443 there, route by SNI vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering, see reverse proxy for MQTT.
  2. Terminate TLS with a certificate for vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering that the tablet trusts. A public certificate is impossible, the name belongs to reMarkable. Use proxy.crt and proxy.key from /home/root/rmfakecloud/ on the tablet: they are valid for *.cloud.remarkable.engineering and signed by the CA that rmfakecloud-proxy installed on the tablet.

docs.title: Tablet
docs.text:
Point the hostname to <your rmfakecloud ip> in the tablet's /etc/hosts. Use the address where port 443 reaches step 1, usually your public IP, not 127.0.0.1: rmfakecloud-proxy on the tablet only handles HTTP. A DNS override on your router usually doesn't help, the tablet asks public DNS servers directly.

On the reMarkable Paper Pro / is read only and /etc is an overlay in RAM, so a plain edit of /etc/hosts is gone after a reboot. Write to the root file system underneath:

mount -o remount,rw /
mkdir -p /tmp/rootfs && mount --bind / /tmp/rootfs
echo "<your rmfakecloud ip> vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering" >> /tmp/rootfs/etc/hosts
umount /tmp/rootfs && mount -o remount,ro /

Like the rmfakecloud-proxy setup, the entry is gone after a system update.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
Start screen sharing on the tablet. The rmfakecloud log shows MQTT: Authentication SUCCESS for the tablet, and the web UI's screen share page picks up the stream.

If nothing shows up in the log, the tablet still reaches reMarkable: check the hosts entry with ping vernemq-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering on the tablet, it has to resolve to <your rmfakecloud ip>.

docs.title: Reenabling after a system update
docs.text: After a system update, you'll need to go through the steps to setup your device again, as any changes you made to it's configuration will have been lost.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
After you installed the proxy, you will need to login to your account on your device.

  1. Click Menu > General > Account.
  2. Click on Setup Account.
  3. On your main computer:
    1. Login to the rmfakecloud Web UI (if no proxy used, the same as the STORAGE_URL value in the server configuration).
    2. Open Connect in the menu, it shows a one time code.
  4. Enter the code on your device.
  5. To check that sync is working correctly. Go to Menu > Storage and press Check Sync.

docs.title: Diff Sync
docs.text:
Since the reMarkable 2.10 release, there is a new sync method available: It collects only differences instead of uploading the whole document. So it takes less time to upload/download large modified documents, and it handles edition conflicts.

Note

This feature is available since rmfakecloud v0.0.5.

New users use it by default. Users created before v0.0.5 need to activate it:

rmfakecloud setuser -u ddvk -s

Add -a for an admin: setuser removes the admin permission if it is not set.

You'll then need to reconnect on your device to apply the settings, and a full resync will automatically begin.

docs.title: Deal with file lost
docs.text:
There was an issue with rmapi affecting both official cloud and rmfakecloud, where files were randomly lost.

The files were not deleted on rmfakecloud side, it was possible to relink them in the real document tree.

Two utility have been designed to help to relink:

  • history2git15: it creates a git repository of the states of the tree, creating a commit for each generation/tree modification.
  • relinkfile15: given an user and an root index name (it's sha256 hash as seen in .root.history or as commit subject of history2git15), it'll relink all files given as argument in their state at the time of the given root index.

Warning

Before using those utilities, please shutdown your rmfakecloud instance to avoid concurrent modifications and possible corruptions.

docs.title: history2git15
docs.text:
Before using history2git15, you need to install git on your system.

This utility takes as argument a path to a .root.history file. It'll create an history directory, which will contain the git repository.

./history2git15 /var/lib/rmfakecloud/users/ddvk/sync/.root.history

As it can takes a large amount of time, you can limit to the latest modifications with the -tail option:

./history2git15 -tail 20 /var/lib/rmfakecloud/users/ddvk/sync/.root.history

In this example only the last 20 modifications of the tree will be saved as a git repository.

After a successfull run, go to /var/lib/rmfakecloud/users/ddvk/sync/history and use git to explore the differences referenced in the two files:

  • doctree: this is a human readable hiereachy of the directories and files, along with the date of the last modification.
  • tree: this is the whole tree state with all metadata accessible, in JSON format.

docs.title: relinkfile15
docs.text:
Warning

Be sure that rmfakecloud is stopped before using this command. Bad things will happen if some devices performs synchronization while relinkfile15 works.

This utility can relink in the root tree a non-deleted file.

DATADIR=/var/lib/rmfakecloud ./relinkfile15 -user ddvk -root-hash 1c0ee6fb7fde7d09dd25b954dd9f23f950d9e25f1fbc661ca18aebf40bb14a00 "Notebook 42" "My calendar.pdf"

DATADIR is the same option used by rmfakecloud. If you don't use it with rmfakecloud, make sure you are in the same directory as when you start rmfakecloud: you should have a data/ directory.

The -user option is the registration address used (or the name of the directory inside data/users).

The -root-hash is the name of the file to use as the old root index.

The rest of the arguments given to the command line are the name of the file as given by history2git15 in doctree (or as visibleName in tree). This doesn't handle directories hierarchy at the time of writing: it only matches the filename. You need to make sure the parent directory still exists (as we said the hierarchy is handle by metadata, not by indexes).

docs.title: How does it work?
docs.text:
All files are saved with a sha256 name in the user sync directory. File can be raw pages, document metadata, directory metadata, indexes, ...

Each file is saved along with a generation number. Each modification increment this generation number.

docs.title: Root tree file
docs.text:
All files in the tree are indexed in a root index. The index references all the index to others files and directories.

The hierarchy is given by each file metadata. The root index file doesn't handle file hierarchy.

docs.title: Current root file in use
docs.text: It is possible to retrieve the current root index in use by consulting the content of the file root. It contains the name of the file containing the root index.

docs.title: History and generation
docs.text: Previous root indexes are kept in the directory and can be listed with the file .root.history. Each line corresponds to a given generation (line 1 = generation 1, ...) and contains the date of the modification and the corresponding filename.

docs.title: File indexes
docs.text:
Each file, as seen on the tablet, is split in several parts (metadata, raw pages, cached transcripted text, content, ...). File indexes store the references of each sub-file.

Files on the tablet are referenced by an UUID. On rmfakecloud files parts are also stores with sha256 names.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Integration is the feature added in reMarkable 2.10 that allows to browse, download and upload document from location outside of the tablet.

Add and edit your integrations on the Integrations page of the web UI. They are stored in your .userprofile.

Warning

The rmfakecloud server connects to the WebDAV, FTP, ICS and webhook addresses, not the tablet. Every user can enter any address, including services in the server's own network (router, NAS, admin interfaces). If you host users you don't fully trust, limit the server's outgoing connections with a firewall or a separate docker network.

docs.title: WebDAV
docs.text:
Any WebDAV service, for example a Nextcloud/Owncloud instance.

Field Description Address WebDAV url, e.g. https://home.example.com/remote.php/dav/files/user42/ Username / Password Credentials for the WebDAV service Insecure Skip the certificate check

docs.title: FTP
docs.text: Field Description Address FTP server, e.g. ftp.example.com:21. Prefix ftps:// for implicit TLS, ftpes:// for explicit TLS Username / Password Credentials for the FTP server Active transfers Use active instead of passive mode

docs.title: Dropbox
docs.text: Field Description Access Token A Dropbox access token, created in the Dropbox App Console

docs.title: Local File System
docs.text:
Warning

Experimental and not suited for multiple users yet

You can share a dedicated path on your system. This can be a simple directory or a mount point using FUSE or whatever. The tablet can't access anything outside of this path.

For security reasons the web UI can't create or edit this integration, it shows the entry to add to your .userprofile instead:

integrations:
  - provider: localfs
    id: [generate some uuid]
    name: [some name]
    path: /some/path/with/files

docs.title: ICS Calendar
docs.text:
Shows a calendar from an ICS url on the tablet.

Field Description ICS URL Url of the .ics file Insecure Skip the certificate check

docs.title: Messaging webhook
docs.text:
Messaging are a type of integration added in software 3.17.

Originally designed for Slack, this feature allows you to send your current sheet as an attachment to a Slack Canvas. The default behavior uses AI to transcribe the handwritten content on your sheet and posts both the text and the image to Slack.

The Webhook integration extends this capability by sending your sheet to an external automation platform (like n8n, Make.com, ...) or custom service. This is especially useful if you want to: use your own AI pipeline or don't want AI to be involved at all, or store and process sheets in a custom backend, ...

Field Description Endpoint Url that receives a multipart POST with the metadata (data) and the sheet as PNG (attachment)

The webhook gives you full control: you decide what happens with your data.

docs.title: Passcode (PIN) Reset
docs.text:
If you forget the passcode on your tablet, the reMarkable lockscreen offers a Forgot PIN flow that asks the cloud to approve the reset. rmfakecloud implements the same flow so you can recover a locked device without needing the official cloud.

Device support

This flow only exists on reMarkable 1 and reMarkable 2. Later devices use a recovery code or a factory reset.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. After several incorrect passcode attempts, an option that says swipe to unlock will appear at the bottom of your screen. Swipe this and then press Reset passcode.
  2. Follow the instructions on your device, and go to your rmfakecloud web UI on your computer and log in to your account.
  3. A banner appears at the top of every page showing the pending reset request for your device — click Approve.
  4. Your old passcode has been reset. Enter a new passcode on your reMarkable.

If the request wasn't initiated by you, click Dismiss instead — the request is removed from rmfakecloud and the tablet will no longer be able to complete the reset for that attempt.

Pending requests are kept in memory only and expire after 24 hours. If the rmfakecloud container restarts before you approve, just tap Forgot PIN again on the tablet to create a fresh request.

docs.title: User Profile
docs.text: Have a look inside data directory (DATADIR): you'll find under data/users/ a directory by user (since v0.0.3). The directory name is expected to be the username given in the webUI login form.

docs.title: User Settings
docs.text:
rmfakecloud stores user configuration (password, email, options, ...) in a file inside its directory, named .userprofile. This is a hidden file.

This file, written in YAML, have the following relevant entries:

Entry Description password Password to access the account (in Argon2 format) name Name displayed in the webui isadmin Boolean indicating if the user can perform administration tasks (currently managing user accounts) sync15 Boolean value that indicates if the user is using the diff synchronization (aka. sync 1.5) integrations Array with the user integrations. See Integrations totpsecret Secret for the two-factor login, only present if it is enabled tokensvalidafter Web UI sessions started before this time are invalid, set on every password change

docs.title: Edit settings through CLI
docs.text:
Use the same binary as for launching the server: it takes some specials commands described bellow.

When using the Docker image, you can run :

docker exec rmfakecloud /rmfakecloud-docker special-command

docs.title: rmfakecloud listusers
docs.text: This commands lists existing users.

docs.title: rmfakecloud setuser
docs.text:
This commands edit or create account.

To create/update an admin account ddvk:

rmfakecloud setuser -u ddvk -a

To reset a password:

read -s -p "New password: " NEWPASSWD && rmfakecloud setuser -u ddvk -p "${NEWPASSWD}"

docs.title: rmfakecloud disabletotp
docs.text:
This command turns off the two-factor login of a user, e.g. after losing the phone:

rmfakecloud disabletotp -u ddvk

docs.title: Two-factor login
docs.text:
Every user can enable a second factor for the web UI login on the profile page: scan the QR code with an authenticator app (any app supporting TOTP) and enter the code it shows. From then on, the login asks for the current code after the password. Disabling it on the profile page also requires a code.

Tablets are not affected: they are paired with a code from the web UI.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
In a user directory, there are files like [UUID].metadata and [UUID].zip (if you are not using sync 1.5): this corresponds to your raw documents on your tablet.

There is also a trash directory, containing deleted files on the tablet, in its trash.

If you are using sync 1.5, the magic happen in the sync directory.
